subject: Production deploy freeze window + ephemeral CI runner attestation request
messages:
From: Ellen Vogt <ellen.vogt@auditsuite.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Financial Audit Team <audit-team@acme-fin.com>
Date: 2025-11-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Evidence request — deploy freeze & CI runner attestation

Irene —

Thanks again for taking this on. As part of our SIG/SOC2 intake for Acme Financial we need a short bundle of SDLC artefacts focused on production deploy governance and ephemeral CI runner hardening. Can you please provide the following by 2025-11-21?

- Production deploy freeze policy (documented windows, exception process).
- Short runbook that demonstrates a rollback (step-by-step for a full release rollback).
- Evidence that CI ephemeral runners are hardened and ephemeral (how images are built, image mutation policy, token/credential TTL and attestation).
- Git commit-signing policy + a sample extract of signed commits for the last 90 days.
- Merge queue / gated merge logs showing enforcement for a representative service (last 90 days).

Prefer attachments in PDF/CSV/TXT. If anything is too sensitive, a redacted extract and a secure link is fine. Also note if any items will be provided via a secure share (Drive/S3 link) rather than attached.

Thanks — specific filenames requested (helpful for tracking): deploy-freeze-policy.pdf, runbook-deploy-rollback.md, ephemeral-runner-attestation.pdf, git-signatures-summary.csv, merge-queue-extract-90d.csv.

—Ellen
Ellen Vogt
Senior Assessor, AuditSuite
ellen.vogt@auditsuite.com
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ellen Vogt <ellen.vogt@auditsuite.com>
Date: 2025-11-14T09:35:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request — deploy freeze & CI runner attestation

Thanks Ellen — assigning internally and we'll aim to meet the 11/21 deadline. Quick split: Jonas, can you own the ephemeral runner attestation, image build provenance, and the git-signature extract? Please include the key rotation log and where KMS/HSM material is stored. Lauren, can you pull the deploy freeze policy and the rollback runbook and include the calendar snapshots and who approves exceptions.

Notes for the bundle:
- We will provide a redacted merge-queue log (no customer PII) and host the full log on our secure bucket under a short-lived signed URL.
- Some infra-level evidence (KMS key metadata) may be exported as redacted screenshots; we'll call those out.

Jonas / Lauren, cc'd Ellen to keep the thread historic. If you expect any delay, flag it by EOD tomorrow so we can ask for an extension.

Irene Choi
Sr. Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ellen Vogt <ellen.vogt@auditsuite.com>
Date: 2025-11-14T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request — deploy freeze & CI runner attestation

Irene — assigning my notes and artifacts below. Delivery plan: I will assemble the attestation package and upload artifacts to the secure drive link listed in metadata. Attached are the redacted extracts we can put directly in the email bundle.

Attachments included (attached to this thread and mirrored to secure drive):
- ephemeral-runner-attestation-20251114.pdf — summary of ephemeral runner lifecycle, image build CI job IDs, SBOM hashes, and image signing details.
- git-signatures-summary-20251114.csv — list of commits with signature verification state for core services (redacted author emails).
- merge-queue-extract-90d.csv — redacted merge queue events (timestamp, PR id, gate result).
- deploy-freeze-policy-20251114.pdf — canonical policy doc (contains the weekly freeze windows and exception approval flow).
- runbook-deploy-rollback-20251114.md — step-by-step rollback with links to health-check dashboards and rollback scripts.

Highlights / quick answers (so you have something to review now):
- Runners are ephemeral VMs spun from a golden image built by our pipeline (pipeline job id: infra-image-20251101). Image hashes (SHA256) are listed in the attestation PDF. Images are rebuilt nightly and on every base-OS CVE patch pull — rebuild cadence is nightly with ad-hoc for critical patches.
- Tokens used to provision runners are short-lived (30m) and issued by our internal token broker; no long-lived runner credentials.
- Image signing: images signed with our build key; build key rotations are logged in KMS with rotation events.
- Commit signing policy: enforced via branch protection; signature-required flag is enabled on protected branches. The CSV extract shows signature verification results.

Access notes: the full merge-queue log is stored in a secure S3 bucket (s3://redwood-secure/logs/merge-queue/) — external assessors will receive a time-limited signed URL if needed. Key rotation metadata (KMS) contains sensitive principal ARNs so we will provide redacted screenshots.

If Ellen wants a short write-up of our image rebuild cadence and the CI job IDs that trigger rebuilds I can add a one-page appendix.

Jonas Weber
Engineering Manager, Build & CI
Redwood Inference
From: Ellen Vogt <ellen.vogt@auditsuite.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-11-14T13:46:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request — deploy freeze & CI runner attestation

Jonas / Irene — thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments. I reviewed the attestation PDF and CSV extracts. A quick clarification only: can you confirm the image rebuild cadence (nightly vs triggered by CVE) and whether rebuilds are automated to replace running runners or only for new runner instances? If you can add that one-line clarification to the attestation PDF or as an appendix in the drive link that will close the loop for this item.

Otherwise this looks good and I will route the redacted artifacts to the assessor pack. If anything else is outstanding I'll flag it.

Thanks —
Ellen
